title: WAC 296-46B — WA Electrical Safety Standards
description: Washington State electrical construction rules, NEC amendments, permits, licensing, exams, and enforcement under WAC 296-46B. 30 questions.

questions.question: When will the 2026 NEC replace the currently adopted 2023 NEC edition in Washington State?
choices: January 1, 2026
July 1, 2026
December 31, 2026
January 1, 2027
questions.answer: December 31, 2026
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-010: The 2026 NEC will replace the 2023 edition effective December 31, 2026, as adopted by reference under WAC 296-46B-010.

questions.question: Which of the following NEC Annexes are specifically included in the adoption of the 2023 NEC?
choices: Annexes A, B, and C only
Annexes D, E, and F only
All Annexes A through H
No Annexes are adopted — only the main body of the NEC
questions.answer: Annexes A, B, and C only
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-010: Washington adopts the 2023 NEC (NFPA 70-2023) by reference, including Annexes A, B, and C specifically.

questions.question: What is the Washington-specific definition of 'Administrator'?
choices: The L&I official who issues electrical permits in a given county
The person who qualifies a contractor's license by passing the required exam
A journey level electrician who supervises apprentices on a job site
The foreman designated to oversee a project with more than ten workers
questions.answer: The person who qualifies a contractor's license by passing the required exam
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-100: Washington's definitions supplement NEC Article 100, and 'Administrator' is defined as the person who qualifies a contractor's license by passing the required examination.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B adds GFCI requirements beyond the NEC for which type of location?
choices: Commercial kitchens in restaurants
Dwelling units
Industrial machinery rooms
Outdoor agricultural facilities
questions.answer: Dwelling units
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-210-008(A): Washington adds extra GFCI requirements for dwelling units beyond those required by the NEC. WAC 296-46B-210-008(B) covers other-than-dwelling units separately.

questions.question: How must branch circuits serving common areas in a multi-family building be arranged?
choices: Common area circuits may share the same panel as individual dwelling unit circuits
Common area branch circuits must be on separate circuits from individual dwelling units
Common areas must be served by a dedicated transformer
Common area loads may be split evenly across any dwelling unit panels
questions.answer: Common area branch circuits must be on separate circuits from individual dwelling units
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-210-025: Washington requires that common area branch circuits be on separate circuits from individual dwelling units in multi-family buildings.

questions.question: Ground fault protection testing is required for feeders over 150V to ground in solidly grounded wye systems at or above what ampere rating?
choices: 600 amperes
800 amperes
1000 amperes
1200 amperes
questions.answer: 1000 amperes
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-215-010: Ground fault protection testing is required for feeders over 150V to ground in solidly grounded wye systems rated 1,000 amperes or greater.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B requires what document for certain electrical projects?
choices: A load calculation stamped by a licensed engineer
Feeder diagrams submitted to L&I before permit issuance
A signed affidavit from the property owner
An arc-flash hazard analysis
questions.answer: Feeder diagrams submitted to L&I before permit issuance
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-215-005: Feeder diagrams are required for certain projects and must be submitted to L&I as part of the plan review or permit process.

questions.question: What is Washington's rule regarding concrete-encased grounding electrodes at new buildings on permanent concrete foundations?
choices: They are permitted but not required, consistent with NEC 250.52
They are required only if ground rods exceed 25 ohms resistance
They are MANDATORY — a Washington amendment requiring them at all new buildings on permanent concrete foundations
They are required only for buildings taller than three stories
questions.answer: They are MANDATORY — a Washington amendment requiring them at all new buildings on permanent concrete foundations
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-052: This is a critical Washington amendment. While NEC 250.52 uses 'shall be permitted' language, WAC 296-46B-250-052 makes concrete-encased grounding electrodes MANDATORY at all new buildings on permanent concrete foundations.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowable resistance to earth for a single ground rod, pipe, or plate electrode before a second electrode must be added?
choices: 10 ohms
25 ohms
50 ohms
100 ohms
questions.answer: 25 ohms
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-053(A)(2): Ground rods, pipes, or plate electrodes must have a resistance to earth of 25 ohms or less. If a single rod exceeds 25 ohms, a second electrode must be installed.

questions.question: A grounding electrode conductor subject to physical damage must be protected by which of the following?
choices: Only rigid metallic conduit (RMC) is acceptable
PVC Schedule 40, Schedule 80, or EMT
Rigid metallic conduit, IMC, rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT
Wireways, auxiliary gutters, or surface metal raceways
questions.answer: Rigid metallic conduit, IMC, rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-064: Where a grounding electrode conductor is subject to physical damage, it must be protected by rigid metallic conduit, intermediate metal conduit (IMC), rigid nonmetallic conduit, or EMT.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE regarding grounding electrode conductors after installation?
choices: They must remain accessible for inspection at all times
They must be inspected annually by the electrical inspector
They are not required to be accessible after installation
They must be labeled with a permanent tag identifying their size
questions.answer: They are not required to be accessible after installation
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-068: Grounding electrode conductors are not required to be accessible after installation, meaning they may be buried, encased, or covered without concern for future access.

questions.question: Bonding is required for which system?
choices: Only metallic water piping systems in new construction
All metal piping systems and structural metal frames
Only gas piping within 6 feet of electrical panels
Structural steel in buildings over 50 feet tall
questions.answer: All metal piping systems and structural metal frames
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-250-090: All metal piping systems and structural metal frames shall be bonded under Washington's grounding and bonding requirements.

questions.question: Regarding raceways installed in suspended ceilings, what does Washington require?
choices: Raceways must be attached to the ceiling grid with listed clips
Raceways in suspended ceilings must be supported independently of the ceiling grid
Suspended ceiling raceways may use the ceiling grid as the sole support
Raceways must be installed above the ceiling grid in all cases
questions.answer: Raceways in suspended ceilings must be supported independently of the ceiling grid
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-300: Washington requires that support of raceways in suspended ceilings be independent of the ceiling grid.

questions.question: What is the requirement regarding the location of a service disconnect?
choices: The service disconnect must be located in a locked electrical room
The service disconnect must be at a readily accessible location
The service disconnect may be located in any accessible attic or crawlspace
The service disconnect must be within 10 feet of the utility meter
questions.answer: The service disconnect must be at a readily accessible location
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-230: Washington requires that the service disconnect be located at a readily accessible location.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about annual permits?
choices: Annual permits are not available in Washington; each job requires a separate permit
Annual permits are available for certain classes of work such as industrial maintenance and telecommunications service work
Annual permits cover all electrical work performed by a licensed contractor for one calendar year
Annual permits are only issued to government agencies performing their own maintenance work
questions.answer: Annual permits are available for certain classes of work such as industrial maintenance and telecommunications service work
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-901: Annual permits are available in Washington for certain classes of work, including industrial maintenance and telecommunications service work, rather than requiring a separate permit for each individual job.

questions.question: What is the deadline for a property owner to obtain a permit after an emergency like-in-kind repair?
choices: Within 24 hours of beginning work
By the next business day
Within 3 working days
Within 15 calendar days
questions.answer: By the next business day
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-901: An exception exists for owner emergency like-in-kind repairs — the permit must be obtained by the next business day after work begins.

questions.question: All backbone telecommunications installations require a permit regardless of size. For non-backbone telecom installations on the customer side, a permit is required when the project exceeds how many outlets?
choices: 5 outlets
10 outlets
15 outlets
25 outlets
questions.answer: 10 outlets
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-901: A telecommunications permit is required for projects greater than ten outlets on the customer side. All backbone installations require a permit regardless of size.

questions.question: How are electrical permit and inspection fees generally structured?
choices: Fees are a fixed $500 for every permit regardless of project size
Fees are based on value of installation or a flat fee depending on type of work
Fees are calculated strictly by square footage of the building
Fees are set by the local jurisdiction, not by L&I
questions.answer: Fees are based on value of installation or a flat fee depending on type of work
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-906: The fee schedule established under WAC 296-46B-906 bases fees on the value of installation or a flat fee depending on the type of work.

questions.question: What is the civil penalty for a contractor performing electrical or telecommunications work WITHOUT a valid contractor's license on a SECOND offense?
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-915: The civil penalty schedule for performing electrical or telecom work without a valid contractor's license is: 1st offense $1,000, 2nd offense $2,000, 3rd offense $3,000, subsequent offenses $10,000 each.

questions.question: Under what circumstance may the Department double the civil penalty?
choices: Whenever the contractor is also cited for a safety violation on the same day
For serious noncompliance, up to a maximum doubled penalty of $10,000
Any time the violator has a prior offense within the past 5 years
Only when the work resulted in personal injury or property damage
questions.answer: For serious noncompliance, up to a maximum doubled penalty of $10,000
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-915: The Department may double the civil penalty for serious noncompliance, but the doubled penalty may not exceed $10,000.

questions.question: Which of the following license/certificate type combinations CANNOT be included in a combination specialty administrator certificate?
choices: Specialty Electrician (06) classes combined together
Telecommunications (09) combined with any specialty class
Journey Level (01) combined with Master Electrician (02)
Multiple specialty (06) sub-classes combined with Journey Level (01)
questions.answer: Telecommunications (09) combined with any specialty class
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-920 and WAC 296-46B-925: A combination specialty administrator certificate cannot include telecommunications (09) because telecom administrators renew on a different (two-year) cycle and are not required to provide continuing education information.

questions.question: What minimum insurance coverage for injury or death to multiple persons is required for a telecommunications contractor license?
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-925: Telecommunications contractor licenses require minimum insurance of: $20,000 for property damage, $50,000 per-person injury or death, and $100,000 for multi-person injury or death.

questions.question: When a telecom contractor obtains a license, the original certificate of insurance must name whom as the certificate holder?
choices: The property owner of the first contracted project
The Washington State Department of Labor and Industries (L&I)
The electrical inspection authority having jurisdiction
The surety bond company underwriting the contractor's bond
questions.answer: The Washington State Department of Labor and Industries (L&I)
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-925: The telecommunications contractor license requires an original certificate of insurance naming L&I as the certificate holder.

questions.question: What happens to a contractor's license if the designated administrator or master electrician leaves and is not replaced within the allowed time?
choices: The contractor must stop work but the license remains active for one year
The license is automatically suspended
The contractor is assessed a civil penalty of $1,000 per day
The license is immediately revoked without right of appeal
questions.answer: The license is automatically suspended
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-930: If a contractor's designated administrator or master electrician leaves and is not replaced within the specified time, the contractor's license is suspended.

questions.question: How long does an applicant have after passing the administrator certificate exam to submit the passing report and fees before the passing result expires?
choices: 30 days
60 days
90 days
180 days
questions.answer: 90 days
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-935: An original administrator certificate is issued upon passing the exam, submitting the passing report within 90 days, and paying the required fees.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of specialty work hours (out of a trainee's properly supervised hours) that may count toward eligibility for the six-month unsupervised training certificate?
choices: 2,000 hours
3,500 hours
4,000 hours
5,000 hours
questions.answer: 4,000 hours
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-942: To qualify for the six-month nonrenewable unsupervised training certificate, a journey level (01) trainee must have worked more than 7,000 properly supervised hours, with no more than 4,000 of those hours being specialty work.

questions.question: What three subjects does the electrician examination cover?
choices: Business law, electrical theory, and NEC code
Safety, state electrical code (WAC 296-46B), and electrical theory
Mathematics, blueprint reading, and NEC code
Safety, blueprint reading, and Washington administrative law
questions.answer: Safety, state electrical code (WAC 296-46B), and electrical theory
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-960: The electrician examination covers (1) safety, (2) state electrical code (WAC 296-46B), and (3) electrical theory. Exams are administered through a testing agency contracted by L&I.

questions.question: Which certificate holders are required to complete continuing education for license renewal?
choices: Only master electricians
Journey level and master electricians
All certificate holders including telecommunications installers
Only administrators and specialty electricians
questions.answer: Journey level and master electricians
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-970: Journey level and master electricians are required to complete continuing education for certificate renewal. Notably, telecommunications administrators are NOT required to provide continuing education information for renewal.

questions.question: Which of the following actions may L&I take against a licensee for violations?
choices: Issue citations and civil penalties only; license suspension requires a court order
Issue citations and civil penalties, and suspend or revoke licenses or certificates
Impose criminal fines but not suspend licenses without a hearing board vote
Only refer cases to the county prosecutor for enforcement action
questions.answer: Issue citations and civil penalties, and suspend or revoke licenses or certificates
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-980 and WAC 296-46B-990: L&I has authority to issue citations and civil penalties, and may suspend or revoke licenses and certificates for violations. Licensees have a right to a hearing and an appeals process.

questions.question: Where do appeals of L&I electrical licensing and enforcement decisions go?
choices: Directly to the Washington State Superior Court
To the Washington State Electrical Board
To the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) only
To the county commission in the county where the violation occurred
questions.answer: To the Washington State Electrical Board
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B-995: Appeals of L&I decisions are directed to the board, which has defined composition and hearing procedures for resolving disputes.
